Interface ObservableList<E>

Type Parameters:
E - the type of the elements
All Superinterfaces:
Observable<List<E>>
public sealed interface ObservableList<E> extends Observable<List<E>>
A list that tells its listeners each change, so that a component showing it updates one row rather than all of them.

Observable.get() returns an unmodifiable snapshot of the elements, which never changes afterwards; get(int) and size() read the current elements. Elements are never null.

Each method that modifies the list makes one ListChange: add and addAll give ListChange.Added; remove, and clear on a list that isn't empty, give ListChange.Removed; set gives ListChange.Replaced of one element; setAll gives Replaced(0, previous, new), or Added when the list was empty, or Removed when the new elements are none. A modification that leaves the list equal (List.equals(Object)) makes no change and calls no listener; set and setAll still store the elements they are given, so that the list holds those instances.

A list is thread-safe. Modifications are serialized by a lock that each one holds while it changes the elements and calls the listeners, so listeners see the changes in the order they were made, each with indices that are valid for the list just before it. Reads take the lock too. Listeners, of subscribeChanges(Scope, Consumer) and of Observable.subscribe(Scope, Consumer) alike, are called synchronously on the thread that modifies the list, while it holds the lock, in the order they subscribed: they must be quick. A listener that modifies an observable list, the one it listens to or any other, throws IllegalStateException: its change would reach the other listeners before the one being delivered, and two lists whose listeners modify each other from two threads would deadlock.

Observable.subscribe(Scope, Consumer) listeners receive the new snapshot, and Observable.map(java.util.function.Function) and Observable.combine(Observable, Observable, java.util.function.BiFunction) work on lists as on any observable.

Only core implements observable lists: the interface is sealed, and of(Object...) and copyOf(Collection) make them.
